title: Eternal's Profit Misses Estimates Even as Blinkit Hits Margin Milestone
excerpt: Zomato's parent posted a 268% year-on-year profit jump to ₹92 crore, but a 47% sequential decline and a miss on analyst forecasts overshadowed Blinkit's improving unit economics.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Eternal's Q1 FY27 profit of ₹92 crore missed analyst expectations of ₹258 crore.
  • Revenue surged to ₹20,211 crore, but fell short of the ₹20,439 crore forecast.
  • Blinkit's adjusted EBITDA margin doubled to 0.6%, with net order value up 86% year-on-year.
  • Eternal raised Blinkit's long-term margin guidance to 5-6%, citing improved efficiency.
  • Zomato's food delivery segment saw a 18.8% rise in net order value, continuing its recovery.

  • Eternal reported Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹92 crore, up 268% year-on-year but 47% below the previous quarter and well short of analyst estimates of ₹258 crore.
  • Revenue surged more than 2.5 times to ₹20,211 crore on the back of Blinkit's rapid expansion, though it too missed consensus forecasts.
  • Blinkit's adjusted EBITDA margin doubled to 0.6% of net order value, with net order value jumping 86% year-on-year and 200 new stores added.
  • Management said competition was "predictable" and raised Blinkit's long-term margin guidance toward the higher end of 5–6%.

Eternal Ltd, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, reported a mixed set of first-quarter results on Wednesday, with surging revenue growth marred by a profit that fell well short of market expectations as competition across India's food delivery and quick-commerce sectors continued to bite.

The company posted a consolidated net profit of ₹92 crore ($9.53 million) for the quarter ended June 30, a 268% increase from ₹25 crore in Q1 FY26 — but a 47% sequential decline from ₹174 crore in Q4 FY26. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected ₹258 crore, making the miss significant.

Revenue from operations rose more than 2.5 times year-on-year to ₹20,211 crore, also marginally below consensus estimates of ₹20,439 crore. The top-line surge reflects the dramatic scaling of Blinkit, which now contributes the majority of consolidated revenue following the company's shift to an inventory-led model in quick commerce.

Blinkit Hits a Milestone

The standout was Blinkit's improving unit economics. The quick-commerce arm's adjusted EBITDA margin doubled to 0.6% of net order value during the quarter, up from 0.3% in Q4 FY26. Adjusted EBITDA reached ₹102 crore, validating management's long-standing claim that the business could achieve profitability at scale.

"This is the inflexion investors have been waiting for," said Vaqarjaved Khan, senior fundamental analyst at Angel One, on the Blinkit margin improvement.

Blinkit's net order value surged 86% year-on-year, and the company added 200 net new dark stores during the quarter, taking the total network to 2,443. Chief Financial Officer Akshant Goyal said growth was driven primarily by customers ordering more frequently rather than spending more per order — a pattern that supports long-term retention economics.

Eternal raised its Blinkit margin guidance, saying it now expected long-term adjusted EBITDA margins at the higher end of the previously guided 5–6% range, citing larger stores and improving operating efficiency. It did not provide a timeline.

The elephant in the room was competition. Swiggy's quick-commerce arm Instamart, Amazon and Flipkart's grocery plays, and insurgents like Zepto continue to pour capital into the space. More recently, Swiggy launched Toing and Rapido launched Ownly, both targeting the food delivery market directly.

Founder Deepinder Goyal acknowledged the pressure but struck a measured tone, saying competition had become "more predictable" and that sustained discount-led growth required continuous cash burn that was "difficult to maintain over the long term." The company signalled it would focus on assortment expansion, geographic reach, and supply-chain infrastructure rather than competing primarily on price.

Core food delivery — still marketed under the Zomato brand — continued to recover. Net order value rose 18.8% year-on-year, marking a third consecutive quarter of improvement. The segment's adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 5.5%, producing ₹532 crore in quarterly EBITDA. Average monthly transacting customers reached 25.4 million, up from 20.9 million a year ago.

Eternal's results encapsulate the tension at the heart of India's platform economy: explosive top-line growth coexisting with persistently thin margins. In FY26, the company processed more than $10 billion in annual transactions and Goyal has targeted $20 billion within two years. But translating that scale into durable profitability remains a work in progress — net profit for the full year FY26 was ₹366 crore on revenue of ₹54,364 crore, a net margin of less than 1%.

For investors, the quarter underscores that Blinkit's path to profitability is real but gradual, and that the consolidated bottom line remains hostage to competitive intensity across multiple verticals. Eternal shares were down 1.8% in afternoon trading on Wednesday.
